title: Lark and the Potion Puzzle
markdown:
The sun popped up like a golden balloon, painting the sky with brilliant pinks and oranges! Lark the water tester bounced out of bed, her toes tingling with excitement. Today was the village fete! Laughter tumbled down the lane like a cascade of little bells. Music tinkled from somewhere far off. Lark’s tummy did a happy little flip-flop. The best part of any fete was always the games, but there was one she was a tiny bit wobbly about – the Potion Pour.

She dashed down to the fete grounds, her braids flying behind her. Bright, bouncy banners snapped in the cool, crisp morning breeze. Dewdrops sparkled like tiny diamonds on the grass. Ms. Rowan, with her cheerful, crinkly smile and bright blue apron, was setting up the games. Lark’s bright, curious eyes darted to the Potion Pour table. Oh, dear! Big jars, tiny beakers, wobbly bottles, and chunky jugs! All different shapes and sizes, glinting in the sunshine. Which one held more sparkly pretend potion? It looked so tricky. Too tricky, Lark thought with a tiny sigh. Her shoulders slumped just a tiny bit, like a wilting daisy.

Suddenly, a huge SPLASH! It was Nibbles the otter, zipping through a gurgling stream that snaked right beside the fete grounds. He was happily filling his favorite smooth, hollow log with cool water. Splish! Splash! As he plopped a smooth, round grey stone into the water, Lark watched, fascinated. The water level jumped UP! Another stone went in with a little plink. The water jumped UP again!

"Look, Lark!" chittered Nibbles, dipping his shiny black tail playfully. "My log is getting full!"

Lark giggled at Nibbles’ wiggles, then blinked. The stones, big and round, took up space. They pushed the water higher and higher. She imagined dropping more and more stones into the log. The water would climb, right to the brim! That’s when it clicked. It wasn't just about the log's size, Lark realised, but about how much space was inside it! The stones took up space, pushing the water up. The more stones she pictured, the higher it rose. Lark’s mind buzzed with a brand new, brilliant idea. She watched Nibbles carefully. Different stones made the water rise just a little bit, or quite a lot. Bigger stones pushed the water up more. This was like a puzzle!

She scampered back to the Potion Pour table, her feet barely touching the grass. She picked up a tall, skinny bottle. Then she picked up a short, fat jug, its sides curving out like a happy tummy. Instead of just guessing, Lark closed her eyes and pretended to fill the tall bottle with tiny, shiny pebbles. Then she imagined filling the short jug with the same tiny pebbles. She pictured them tumbling in, filling every nook and cranny. The short, fat jug could hold SO many more pebbles! It clearly had more space inside. It had more capacity. Lark grinned, a big, bright, triumphant grin. She knew!

"Ms. Rowan!" Lark piped up, her voice clear and bright, pointing a determined finger. "This jug holds more than that bottle!"

Ms. Rowan, always ready for a bit of learning, smiled kindly. "That's wonderful, Lark! How do you know?"

"Because," Lark explained, holding up a small, smooth pebble she’d found, "if I filled both with these, the jug would need LOTS and LOTS of pebbles to be full! It holds more space inside!"

Nibbles popped his sleek head out of the stream, his whiskers twitching with eagerness. "Let's try it at the game!" he squeaked, already zipping over.

Together, Lark and Nibbles became the best Potion Pour team the village had ever seen! Lark pointed to the containers that looked like they could hold the most pebbles, the ones with the biggest “tummies.” Nibbles, with his speedy paws and expert otter reflexes, helped pretend to fill them, chittering with delight. They compared a tall, skinny flask that looked elegant to a short, wide pot that looked sturdy. Lark quickly decided the pot held more. Then they looked at a wobbly, round bottle and a straight, tall cylinder. Lark nudged the round bottle with her nose. "This one!" she declared confidently. They pretended to pour their sparkly pretend potion. Their pot was full to the brim, shimmering and bright, while the cylinder was only half-full. They had filled the containers with the most capacity!

"Hooray!" cheered Nibbles, splashing his tail with such force a little rainbow seemed to arc through the air. They’d won the game!

Ms. Rowan clapped her hands, her eyes sparkling. "You two are brilliant at judging capacity!"

Lark beamed, her heart feeling as full as the winning jug. It wasn't just magic or luck; it was understanding how much space things could hold. By looking carefully and comparing how objects could fill up a space, she knew which container was biggest. Lark couldn't wait to explore more of the fete, her mind buzzing with all the clever things she’d discovered. What other secrets were hiding in plain sight? Today was going to be AMAZING!
characters: Lark the water tester, Nibbles the otter, Ms. Rowan
